## Summary

Adds a 24h timeline strip to the Cron Jobs page in the Control UI, providing an at-a-glance view of today's scheduled tasks.

Closes #40644

## Screenshots

### Dark Theme — Full View
![Full page dark](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/xvchris/cron-calendar-screenshots/main/dark-full.jpg)
*Summary strip with always-on chip, 24h timeline with NOW indicator, cluster badges, color-coded dots*

### Cluster Hover — Overlapping Jobs
![Cluster hover](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/xvchris/cron-calendar-screenshots/main/cluster-hover.jpg)
*Hovering the ④ cluster at 22:00 shows 4 overlapping jobs with color-coded dots and times*

### Single Dot Hover — Job Info Popup
![Dot hover](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/xvchris/cron-calendar-screenshots/main/dot-hover.jpg)
*Hovering oss-scan dot shows schedule, status, duration, and "Click → view run history" hint*

### Light Theme
![Light theme](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/xvchris/cron-calendar-screenshots/main/light-theme.jpg)
*Full light theme support via existing CSS variables*

## Features

### Timeline Strip
- **24-hour timeline track** with grid lines and time labels
- **NOW indicator** — red vertical line showing current time, auto-updates every 60s
- **Color-coded dots** — each job gets a distinct color; green for past (ok), blue pulse for future (pending)
- **Cluster badges** — nearby dots (within 2.5%) auto-merge into a numbered badge; hover to see the full list
- **Hover popups** — JS-driven mouseenter/mouseleave with 150ms debounce for reliable hover behavior
- **Click navigation** — past dots jump to Run History (filtered), future dots scroll to job details
- **Zoom controls** — 24h (full day), Work (08:00–20:00), Now±3h (centered on current time)

### Always-On Chips
- High-frequency jobs (every <10min or cron `*/N` where N≤10) are displayed as chips in the summary strip instead of cluttering the timeline
- Hover to see: View Details / View History / Run Now actions
- Click to jump to run history

### Other
- **Mobile fallback** — timeline hidden on narrow screens, replaced by a simple text list of upcoming jobs
- **Full i18n** — all strings use `t()`, translations added for en, zh-CN, zh-TW, de, es, pt-BR
- **Theme support** — uses only existing CSS variables, works in both dark and light modes
- **No existing features removed** — purely additive changes to the view layer

## Files Changed

| File | Change |
|------|--------|
| `ui/src/ui/helpers/cron-timeline.ts` | **New** — Timeline computation (zoom, clustering, high-freq detection) |
| `ui/src/ui/views/cron.ts` | Added timeline rendering between summary and workspace |
| `ui/src/styles/components.css` | Added timeline CSS (523 lines) |
| `ui/src/i18n/locales/*.ts` | Added `cron.timeline.*` keys to all 6 locales |

- Computed timeline data from existing `CronProps` — no controller changes needed
- All new code is additive; existing view functions untouched
- TypeScript strict mode compatible

target.title: feat(agents): per-agent outbound A2A allowlist override
target.body:
## Summary

- Add `agents.list[].tools.agentToAgent.allow` to control which agents a specific agent may contact via session tools (`sessions_send`, `sessions_list`, `sessions_history`, `session_status`)
- When unset, the agent falls back to the global `tools.agentToAgent.allow` list; when set to explicit IDs, only those targets are reachable; `[]` isolates the agent from all cross-agent access
- The global `tools.agentToAgent.allow` continues to act as a participation gate (both requester and target must match it) before per-agent outbound rules are evaluated
- Outbound-only semantics: only the requester's override is checked, not the target's
- Replace `matchesAllow` with `matchesGlobalParticipation` and add `evaluateAccess()` returning a structured `AgentToAgentDenyReason` so all call sites produce context-aware error messages via `formatAgentToAgentAccessError()`
- Scrub deleted agent references from per-agent outbound allowlists in `pruneAgentConfig()`

### Example config (hub-spoke pattern)

```json
{
  "tools": {
    "agentToAgent": { "enabled": true, "allow": ["*"] }
  },
  "agents": {
    "list": [
      { "id": "david",  "tools": { "agentToAgent": { "allow": ["*"] } } },
      { "id": "spoke",  "tools": { "agentToAgent": { "allow": ["david"] } } },
      { "id": "kelly",  "tools": { "agentToAgent": { "allow": ["david"] } } }
    ]
  }
}
```

spoke→david ✅ | spoke→kelly ❌ | david→anyone ✅

## Test plan

- [x] `sessions-access.test.ts`: per-agent override, deny-all `[]`, global gate, target override ignored (outbound-only), fallback to global when unset
- [x] `sessions.test.ts`: per-agent outbound deny during label lookup in `sessions_send`
- [x] `openclaw-tools.session-status.test.ts`: per-agent outbound deny for cross-agent `session_status`
- [x] `agents.test.ts`: `pruneAgentConfig` scrubs deleted agent from per-agent allowlists
- [x] Build passes
- [x] Manual: configure hub-spoke agents (david/spoke/kelly), verify per-agent outbound rules — see `Real behavior proof` section below

## Real behavior proof

- **Behavior or issue addressed**: per-agent outbound `agentToAgent.allow` correctly gates cross-agent session tool access. Hub-spoke topology used: `david` (hub, `allow=["*"]`), `spoke` (allow=`["david"]`), `kelly` (allow=`["david"]`). Validates the new `evaluateAccess()` decision pipeline reaches the documented per-agent outbound semantics, with the structured `per_agent_outbound` deny reason surfaced via `formatAgentToAgentAccessError()`.

- **Real environment tested**: Ubuntu 22.04 (kernel 5.15), Node 22.22.0, pnpm 10. Branch HEAD `55819f6f43` of `repair/pr-39102-a2a-refresh` (this PR rebased on current main). Live invocation of the production export `createAgentToAgentPolicy` from `src/plugin-sdk/session-visibility.ts` — no mocks, no test runner, the same code path that backs `sessions_send`, `sessions_list`, `sessions_history`, and `session_status` at runtime.

- **Exact steps or command run after this patch**:

  1. Author a hub-spoke `OpenClawConfig` matching the docs example (david hub + spoke + kelly).
  2. Build `policy = createAgentToAgentPolicy(cfg)`.
  3. Call `policy.evaluateAccess(requester, target)` for the five edge pairs.
  4. Run with: `pnpm tsx proof-hub-spoke.ts` (the script imports the worktree source directly so the running code is the patched export).

- **Evidence after fix**: terminal output, copied verbatim from `node` stdout via `tsx`.

  ```
  # per-agent A2A allowlist — hub-spoke proof
  # config: david=hub (allow *), spoke=spoke (allow david), kelly=spoke (allow david)

  [ok ] spoke -> david: ALLOWED
  [ok ] spoke -> kelly: DENIED (reason=per_agent_outbound)
  [ok ] david -> kelly: ALLOWED
  [ok ] david -> spoke: ALLOWED

Cross-spoke calls (`spoke -> kelly`, `kelly -> spoke`) were denied with the structured `per_agent_outbound` reason code from `AgentToAgentDecision`. target.title: fix(signal): complete bidirectional quote-reply support
target.body:
## Summary

Adds complete bidirectional Signal quote-reply support — both outbound (agent → user) and inbound (user → agent) quote context handling.

## Problem

**Outbound (agent → user):** When the assistant includes reply tags (`[[reply_to_current]]`, `[[reply_to:<id>]]`), they were stripped but never translated into signal-cli quote parameters. Signal showed no visual reply indicator, unlike Discord/Telegram/Slack.

**Inbound (user → agent):** When a user quote-replies to the agent, the quoted message context was either lost or only used as fallback body text. The agent had no structured awareness of what was being quoted, who wrote it, or that a quote-reply was even happening.

## Solution

### Outbound Changes (agent → user)

1. **Signal outbound adapter** (`src/channels/plugins/outbound/signal.ts`)
   - Updated `sendText()` and `sendMedia()` to pass `replyToId` and `quoteAuthor`

2. **Signal send function** (`src/signal/send.ts`)
   - Added `replyTo` and `quoteAuthor` to `SignalSendOpts`
   - Converts `replyTo` timestamp into signal-cli `quote-timestamp` / `quote-author` RPC params
   - Uses `Number()` instead of `parseInt()` for strict timestamp validation
   - Guards group quotes: skips quoting when `quoteAuthor` is missing (avoids silent signal-cli failures)

3. **Delivery layer** (`src/infra/outbound/deliver.ts`)
   - `trackReplyConsumption` pattern for bestEffort partial-failure handling
   - `sendPayload` branch routes through quote gating
   - Reply metadata consumed only after successful send
   - Per-payload explicit `replyToId` preserved independently of inherited reply

4. **Event handler — outbound** (`src/signal/monitor/event-handler.ts`)
   - `resolveQuotedAuthor()` with LRU cache for group quote-author resolution

target.title: feat(workspace): add tiered bootstrap loading with configurable bootstrapTier
target.body:
Closes #22438

## Motivation

Bootstrap files consume LLM tokens on every session. For users with large workspaces, loading all files into every session — including sub-agents and cron jobs — wastes context window budget on files the agent never references. This PR introduces tiered loading so users can control how much context each session type receives, **reducing unnecessary token usage** while preserving persona consistency where needed.

## What

Introduces a three-tier bootstrap file loading system (`minimal` | `standard` | `full`) with a new `agents.defaults.bootstrapTier` configuration option. Both the `minimal` and `standard` tiers exclude hook-loaded extras (e.g. `packages/*/AGENTS.md` from the `bootstrap-extra-files` hook); `full` keeps everything.

## Why

The current binary split (main=all, subagent/cron=minimal) doesn't support use cases where subagents need persona context or where main sessions should be lightweight. This adds a clean, backward-compatible middle ground that lets users optimize their token budget per session type.

## How

- **`resolveBootstrapTier(sessionKey, tierOverride)`** — resolves the effective tier from session type + optional config override.
- **`filterBootstrapFilesForSession(files, sessionKey, tierOverride)`** — extended with optional tier parameter (backward compatible — no tierOverride = existing session-type heuristic).
- **Hook-source guard** — both `minimal` and `standard` filters check `file.source !== "hook"` before allowlist matching, so a hook-loaded extra whose basename happens to be in the allowlist cannot slip in. This preserves the natural `minimal ⊂ standard ⊂ full` inclusion order on the real hook path.
- **Config** — `agents.defaults.bootstrapTier` in the zod schema, TypeScript types, labels, and help text.

The `source: "root" | "hook"` provenance field on `WorkspaceBootstrapFile` is the discriminator: root-level bootstrap files keep flowing through `minimal` and `standard`; per-package extras registered via the `bootstrap-extra-files` hook are only reachable through `full`.

## Real behavior proof

Behavior or issue addressed: tiered bootstrap loading — `agents.defaults.bootstrapTier` (`minimal` | `standard` | `full`) controls which workspace files are injected into each session's context window. Closes #22438. After the latest fix (`5cdaf8e774`), the legacy no-override default path also applies the `file.source !== "hook"` guard, so subagent and cron sessions stay root-only by default — matching the upstream session-type defaults this PR preserves.

- Tier resolution: subagent and cron sessions default to `minimal`; main defaults to `standard`. Any session honors an explicit `tierOverride`.
- Legacy default no-override path: main = 10 files (all loaded including hook extras), subagent = **2 files** (legacy AGENTS.md + TOOLS.md root only — hook-sourced `packages/*/AGENTS.md` correctly excluded), cron = **5 files** (legacy AGENTS+TOOLS+SOUL+IDENTITY+USER root only — hook-sourced AGENTS.md correctly excluded). The hook-source guard introduced in `5cdaf8e774` closes the gap between `resolveBootstrapTier`'s reported tier and the actual filter output.
- Explicit `tier="minimal"`: 5 files (MINIMAL_BOOTSTRAP_ALLOWLIST root only). Hook-sourced files always excluded.
- Explicit `tier="standard"`: 8 files (STANDARD_BOOTSTRAP_ALLOWLIST root only). Hook-sourced files always excluded.
- Explicit `tier="full"`: 10 files (all loaded including hook extras).

target.title: fix(cli): strip reseed wrapper from imported CLI session messages
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes #99646. When the CLI-runner reseeds a fresh `claude-cli` session from the OpenClaw transcript, the internal reseed prompt envelope ("Continue this conversation using the OpenClaw transcript…") was imported as a regular user message and rendered as a user chat bubble.

## Root Cause / Fix

`parseClaudeCliHistoryEntry` imports every user-type JSONL entry without filtering. The reseed wrapper built by `buildCliSessionHistoryPrompt` ends up as a user message in the native CLI session file, and the gateway history import passes it through to the chat display.

**Fix**: Detect the reseed envelope with a regex and extract only the real user message. Three cases:
- Match with real message → return stripped message
- Match with empty message → drop the entry
- No match → pass through unchanged

Changes (2 files, +117 lines):
- `src/gateway/cli-session-history.claude.ts`: `CLI_RESEED_ENVELOPE_RE` + `stripCliReseedEnvelope()`
- `src/gateway/cli-session-history.test.ts`: 3 tests

## Evidence

### Real Live Proof (production CLI session)
```
$ node --import tsx live-proof.ts
Total: 1100 messages, wrapper=0 real_user=110
PASS: wrapper stripped in real session
```
Verified against a real 1100-message CLI session containing reseed wrappers. Zero leaked wrappers.

### Production Function Proof
```
$ node --import tsx proof.ts
Messages after import: 2
  [user] CHECK: deployment status?
  [user] normal message
PASS: wrapper stripped — only real messages remain
```

### Test Runner
```
$ node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/gateway/cli-session-history.test.ts
 Test Files  4 passed (4)
      Tests  88 passed (88)   (+3 new: extract, drop empty, passthrough)
```

### Autoreview + Formatting
```
autoreview → patch is correct (0.95)
oxfmt --check → clean  |  oxlint → clean  |  git diff --check → clean
```

## Change Type
- `fix` — bug fix for CLI session history import

## Security Impact
- None. Regex matching on imported text; no new permissions, network, or dependency changes.

target.title: fix(channels): retain failed ingress payloads
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Failed ingress-queue tasks could lose the original payload when they were serialised for failure/dead-letter handling. For Telegram/forum-topic ingress, that makes some missed updates unrecoverable: the system can see that work failed, but no longer has the original update needed to inspect, replay, or recover the prompt.

## Summary

- keep the original ingress queue payload available when a queued message fails
- preserve recoverability for dead-lettered Telegram/forum-topic updates
- keep old failed tombstones that stored `payload_json` as literal JSON `null` plugin-visible without `payload: null`
- add regression coverage for failed task serialisation and old failed tombstones

## Evidence

- `src/channels/message/ingress-queue.test.ts` adds coverage that a failed task keeps the original payload while recording the failure.
- `src/channels/message/ingress-queue.test.ts` adds coverage that old failed tombstones with cleared payload storage omit `payload` instead of exposing `payload: null`.
- After-fix focused test: `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/channels/message/ingress-queue.test.ts` -> 1 file passed, 17 tests passed.
- After-fix redacted runtime smoke with a Telegram/forum-topic-shaped ingress payload recovered the original failed payload on duplicate enqueue:

```json
{
  "kind": "failed",
  "duplicate": true,
  "reason": "handler-error",

  "forumTopicId": "redacted-topic"

target.title: feat(google): restore Antigravity and harden Gemini auth boundary
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

This PR restores first-class Google auth replacement support for the three Google provider paths that currently matter:

- `google-antigravity` uses the signed-in Antigravity/`agy` session and runs prompts through `agy --print`.
- `google-gemini-cli` imports the official Gemini CLI OAuth cache and validates the active account identity before using it.
- `google` remains the Gemini API-key provider.

The important boundary is that Google credentials stay provider-owned. OpenClaw does not start its own Google browser callback for Antigravity, and it does not import or persist raw Google OAuth tokens from Antigravity. For Antigravity, OAuth/session ownership stays with the Antigravity/`agy` session.

This also hardens the shared Google auth replacement boundary. Gemini CLI OAuth cache import now requires validated active Google account identity before credential material is saved, refreshed, forwarded, or staged. Legacy `google-gemini-cli` OAuth profiles missing account identity are recovered through the official Gemini CLI cache when the imported account matches the expected profile identity; otherwise they fail closed.

## What Changed

Antigravity:

- Added bundled `google-antigravity` provider registration.
- Added a `google-antigravity` CLI backend.
- Routed `google-antigravity` prompts through `agy --print` with a bounded print timeout.
- Added Antigravity setup that creates a local `google-antigravity:antigravity-session` auth profile from the signed-in Antigravity app/session boundary.
- Added runtime auth resolution for the Antigravity app-session profile.
- Added external/synthetic auth handling so OpenClaw can identify the Antigravity session without importing raw Google OAuth tokens.
- Added Antigravity provider aliases and Google provider model/policy wiring.
- Updated setup notes to make the boundary explicit: Antigravity owns the Google OAuth session; OpenClaw delegates execution to `agy`.

Gemini CLI:

- Added official Gemini CLI cache import support for `google-gemini-cli`.
- Changed `google-gemini-cli` setup to import the official Gemini CLI cache instead of launching an OpenClaw-owned Google browser auth flow.
- Required validated active Gemini CLI Google account identity during cache import.
- Added compatibility handling for legacy `google-gemini-cli` OAuth profiles that lack identity by recovering identity from the official Gemini CLI cache when it matches the expected profile.
- Failed closed when Gemini CLI account identity is missing or mismatched.
- Failed closed before save, refresh, forwarding, or runtime staging when account identity does not match.
- Preserved isolated Gemini CLI auth-home staging.
- Preserved inherited Google auth env clearing.

Shared auth/backend boundary:

- Added provider-owned CLI backend auth resolution through `resolveCliBackendAuthCredential`.
- Preserved generic fallback forwarding only when no provider-owned hook exists.
- Made provider hook decline fail closed instead of falling through to generic forwarding.
- Preserved backend allowlist checks before and after auth resolution.
- Preserved Gemini API-key staging for `google` API-key profiles.
- Fixed CLI runner cleanup gaps on mid-prepare failures.
- Updated Google provider docs, live-testing docs, Plugin SDK exports/API baseline, and CLI backend plugin docs.

## Evidence

Antigravity headless behavior:

```text
agy -h
agy models
agy --print 'Reply exactly: OPENCLAW_AGY_PRINT_OK' --print-timeout 2m0s
```

Result: `agy --print` returned `OPENCLAW_AGY_PRINT_OK`.

Sterile-home Antigravity session behavior:

```text
HOME="$PROOF_HOME" ANTIGRAVITY_USER_DATA_DIR="$HOME/.config/Antigravity" agy --print 'Reply exactly: OPENCLAW_AGY_STERILE_OK' --print-timeout 2m0s
```

Result: `agy --print` returned `OPENCLAW_AGY_STERILE_OK` while running under the isolated proof `HOME`. This verifies that the runtime can use the Antigravity session boundary through `ANTIGRAVITY_USER_DATA_DIR` instead of relying on the operator's normal home directory.

OpenClaw Antigravity runtime behavior:

```text
HOME="$PROOF_HOME" \
OPENCLAW_CONFIG_PATH="$PROOF_CONFIG" \
ANTIGRAVITY_USER_DATA_DIR="$HOME/.config/Antigravity" \
pnpm openclaw qa manual \
  --provider-mode live-frontier \
  --model google-antigravity/gemini-3-flash \
  --message 'Reply exactly: OPENCLAW_AGY_OPENCLAW_OK' \
  --timeout-ms 240000
```

Result: OpenClaw returned status `ok` with reply `OPENCLAW_AGY_OPENCLAW_OK`.

Focused validation:

```text
pnpm test extensions/google/index-harness-registration.test.ts extensions/google/setup-api.test.ts extensions/google/index.test.ts src/agents/cli-backends.test.ts src/agents/cli-runner/prepare.test.ts
```

Result: passed. Agents shard: 87 tests passed. Extension-providers shard: 32 tests passed. Total focused tests: 119 passed.

```text
pnpm check:test-types
```

Result: passed.

```text
pnpm plugin-sdk:api:check
```

Result: passed. `OK docs/.generated/plugin-sdk-api-baseline.sha256`.

```text
pnpm plugin-sdk:surface:check
```

Result: passed. Public SDK surface check passed with no package-exported forbidden subpaths.

```text
git diff --check
```

Result: passed.

Gemini CLI behavior:

- Official Gemini CLI cache import through OpenClaw succeeds and creates a `google-gemini-cli/<account>` OAuth profile from the official cache.
- OpenClaw runtime reaches the `google-gemini-cli` OAuth path when invoked with a `google-gemini-cli/...` model ref.
- The live Gemini CLI account used for proof is blocked upstream by Google's `IneligibleTierError`/unsupported-client gate. A direct official `gemini` CLI control run hits the same upstream eligibility gate, which confirms the remaining failure is upstream account/client eligibility rather than OpenClaw auth routing.

## Owner Acceptance

Provider owner acceptance: pending.

Plugin SDK owner acceptance: pending.

Security owner acceptance: pending.

Maintainer acceptance for the Google auth replacement boundary and provider-owned credential handling: pending.

## What Was Not Tested

I did not run the full repository test suite. The focused suites cover the changed Google provider registration, Antigravity setup/runtime behavior, Gemini CLI account identity validation, CLI auth forwarding boundary, types, SDK surface, and proof behavior.

I did not prove successful Gemini CLI model generation with the live account. The changed OpenClaw path reaches Gemini CLI OAuth runtime, but the installed official Gemini CLI and account are blocked by Google's upstream unsupported-client/eligibility gate.

I did not prove model-specific Antigravity selection through `agy --model`. The current Antigravity proof shows that OpenClaw routes `google-antigravity/gemini-3-flash` through the `agy --print` runtime and receives a response. A follow-up can map OpenClaw model refs to exact `agy models` display names and pass `--model` explicitly.

The targeted gateway live harness still has a known limitation for explicit provider-scoped sweeps: that path suppresses external/synthetic auth profiles during auth preflight before CLI backend execution. The product/runtime proof is therefore captured with `pnpm openclaw qa manual`, which reaches the actual `google-antigravity` backend and returns the expected response.

## Tests

AI-assisted: yes.

## Real behavior proof

Latest Antigravity proof files:

- `/home/rev/pr-98343-antigravity-current-proof/15-agy-headless-print-proof.txt`
- `/home/rev/pr-98343-antigravity-current-proof/16-agy-sterile-home-proof.txt`
- `/home/rev/pr-98343-antigravity-current-proof/17-openclaw-agy-runtime-proof.txt`

Real Antigravity behavior proven:

- `agy -h` exposes non-interactive `--print` mode and `--print-timeout`.
- `agy models` lists the Antigravity model surface.
- Direct `agy --print 'Reply exactly: OPENCLAW_AGY_PRINT_OK'` returns `OPENCLAW_AGY_PRINT_OK`.
- `agy --print` works under a sterile proof `HOME` when `ANTIGRAVITY_USER_DATA_DIR` points at the signed-in Antigravity session.
- OpenClaw `qa manual --model google-antigravity/gemini-3-flash` routes through the `google-antigravity` backend and returns `OPENCLAW_AGY_OPENCLAW_OK`.
- OpenClaw does not import or persist raw Google OAuth tokens for Antigravity. OAuth/session ownership stays with the Antigravity/`agy` session.

Real Gemini CLI behavior proven:

- OpenClaw imports the official Gemini CLI OAuth cache through the `google-gemini-cli` setup path.
- OpenClaw validates the imported account identity before saving or using the profile.
- Legacy identity-missing `google-gemini-cli` profiles can recover through the official cache when the imported identity matches the expected profile.
- Mismatched or missing identity fails closed.
- OpenClaw reaches the changed `google-gemini-cli` OAuth runtime path; the live account is then blocked by Google's upstream unsupported-client/eligibility gate, matching the direct official Gemini CLI control failure.

target.body:
## Summary
- expose default-disabled `core/doctor/legacy-cron-store` findings for legacy cron stores, legacy run logs, quarantined rows, SQLite projection backfills, legacy notify fallback, and stale dreaming payload shape
- use read-only state inspection paths for selected lint
- keep all real cron mutation in the existing legacy cron `doctor --fix` contribution; this PR is lint-only and does not add a structured repair/dry-run hook

## Contract / compatibility
- No public SDK, plugin, config, or CLI contract changes.
- Default `doctor --lint` is unchanged; `--only core/doctor/legacy-cron-store` and `--all` can select it.
- Selected lint must not create or rewrite user cron state.

## Validation on `9ca7491f8c`
- `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/commands/doctor/cron/index.test.ts src/flows/doctor-health-contributions.test.ts` (119 tests)
- changed-file `oxfmt --check`
- changed-file `oxlint --tsconfig config/tsconfig/oxlint.core.json`
- `pnpm check:architecture`
- `node scripts/plugin-sdk-surface-report.mjs --check`
- `git diff --check`

## Type-check note
- Hosted `check-test-types` on `56a56afdc5` failed on an untyped test mock; fixed on `9ca7491f8c` by typing `collectLegacyCronStoreHealthFindings` as `Promise<readonly HealthFinding[]>`.
- Local Windows `pnpm check:test-types` / `pnpm tsgo:core:test` timed out without diagnostics after the fix; hosted CI is the authoritative type-check proof for the refreshed head.

## Real behavior proof on `56a56afdc5` (source behavior unchanged on `9ca7491f8c`)
- Ran source CLI with isolated `OPENCLAW_CONFIG_PATH` and `OPENCLAW_STATE_DIR` against a temp legacy cron JSON array store:
  `node scripts/run-node.mjs doctor --lint --json --only core/doctor/legacy-cron-store`
- Result: exit code 1, `checksRun: 1`, `checksSkipped: 44`, four `core/doctor/legacy-cron-store` warning findings for the temp legacy store.
- Read-only proof: `<state>/openclaw-state.sqlite` was not created and `<state>/identity/device.json` was not created.

## Notes
The earlier structured dry-run preview text was removed after Omar's review because the core check repair hook was not reachable from a supported Doctor CLI path. Real mutation remains in the legacy cron `doctor --fix` path.

target.title: fix: estimate DeepSeek spend when API reports zero cost
target.body:
Closes #97047

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where users running DeepSeek V4 models would see Control UI Spend stay at zero when the DeepSeek API recorded nonzero token usage but returned `usage.cost.total: 0`.

## Why This Change Was Made

When transcript scanning sees nonzero token usage, a recorded zero provider total, and known positive model pricing, OpenClaw now recomputes the session cost from pricing instead of treating the provider total as authoritative. The durable usage-cost cache version is bumped so previously cached zero-spend summaries are rebuilt under the corrected semantics.

## User Impact

DeepSeek V4 usage with known pricing now contributes to session and Control UI spend totals instead of appearing as confident zero-cost activity. Unknown/all-zero pricing still surfaces as missing cost rather than guessing spend.

target.title: test(qa): redact script evidence diagnostics
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

QA script producers persist bounded child-process diagnostics as evidence. If stdout or stderr is tailed before redaction, a discarded prefix can remove the context required to recognize a credential while leaving its sensitive suffix in the saved artifact. Configured logging patterns can also span the shared redactor's normal internal chunk boundary.

## Why This Change Was Made

This change keeps one redaction contract instead of introducing producer-specific secret APIs:

- adds an internal full-context variant of the existing tool-payload redactor for callers that have already bounded raw input;
- buffers QA evidence only up to a fixed safe limit, then redacts before taking the persisted tail;
- omits oversized raw logs and failure details rather than truncating before redaction;
- streams hosted-media and ClawHub child output into the evidence writer before their parsing/status buffers discard data;
- retains the existing built-in and configured `logging.redactPatterns` behavior.

The regression crosses both child stream chunks and the shared redactor's 16 KiB boundary with a configured pattern.

## User Impact

There is no product runtime behavior change. QA evidence remains bounded while avoiding secret-bearing tails caused by pre-redaction truncation.

## Evidence

- `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/logging/redact.test.ts test/e2e/qa-lab/runtime/script-evidence.test.ts test/e2e/qa-lab/media/hosted-media-provider-live.test.ts test/e2e/qa-lab/plugins/clawhub-release-candidate-install.test.ts` — 140 tests passed across two Vitest shards.
- Blacksmith Testbox through Crabbox `tbx_01kwmw3czcxyb7qj0x5r1gvnn8` — changed type, lint, guard, and import-cycle checks passed; hydration run: https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/28682925039.
- Codex autoreview of the final local patch — clean, no accepted/actionable findings.

target.title: fix: preserve OpenCode Go DeepSeek V4 max thinking
target.body:
Closes #99601

AI-assisted: yes (Codex).

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where users selecting `/think max` or `/think xhigh` with `opencode-go/deepseek-v4-pro` or `opencode-go/deepseek-v4-flash` would have the requested thinking level silently clamped down before the OpenCode Go DeepSeek V4 request was built.

## Why This Change Was Made

The OpenCode Go DeepSeek V4 model rows now carry an explicit thinking-level map in both runtime catalog data and manifest metadata: `off` disables thinking, normal levels map to DeepSeek's low/medium/high efforts, and `xhigh`/`max` map to DeepSeek's max effort. The fix stays inside the opencode-go provider metadata so the existing generic clamp and DeepSeek V4 OpenAI-compatible stream wrapper continue to own their current behavior.

## User Impact

OpenCode Go DeepSeek V4 users can use max/xhigh thinking and have the request reach the provider as max effort instead of being downgraded to high. Static model discovery and runtime provider discovery now agree on the same DeepSeek V4 thinking capabilities.

## Evidence

- `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs extensions/opencode-go/index.test.ts` (12 passed)
- `git diff --check`
- GitHub `Real behavior proof` context/evidence gate passed: https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/28680430416

target.title: fix: keep OpenClaw control tools available when tool_search misroutes
target.body:
Closes #99464
Related: #99551

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where Codex app-server workers could be told to discover OpenClaw session/control tools through `tool_search`, but `tool_search` could resolve a different connector universe and leave the worker without the OpenClaw delegation/control tools it needed.

## Why This Change Was Made

OpenClaw now keeps the critical control-path dynamic tools, `heartbeat_respond`, `sessions_spawn`, and `sessions_yield`, in the direct Codex tool surface while leaving broad OpenClaw tools deferred/searchable. This preserves Codex-native `spawn_agent` as the recommended Codex-subagent path in developer instructions, but removes the unsafe dependency on a successful deferred search result for OpenClaw/ACP delegation and heartbeat handling.

Codex source inspection for this change used sibling `../codex` at `da4c8ca57d40b074bdc1b5b1218851100150c56b`:

- `codex-rs/app-server/README.md:1557-1566` documents that deferred dynamic functions must be namespaced and are searchable only when `tool_search` is available.
- `codex-rs/core/src/tools/spec_plan.rs:494-536` enables deferred-tool guidance only when the search tool is enabled.
- `codex-rs/core/src/tools/spec_plan.rs:964-984` builds `tool_search` only from planned deferred runtimes with search info.
- `codex-rs/core/src/tools/handlers/tool_search.rs:74-87` builds the search index from the supplied deferred-tool search infos.

## User Impact

OpenClaw Codex workers keep access to OpenClaw heartbeat and session delegation controls even when deferred `tool_search` is unavailable or returns unrelated connector results. Operators should see fewer fallbacks to expensive raw shell inspection when an OpenClaw worker needs OpenClaw-specific session controls.

## Evidence

- `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs extensions/codex/src/app-server/dynamic-tools.test.ts`
  - 81 tests passed.
- `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs extensions/codex/src/app-server/run-attempt.test.ts`

target.title: fix: fall back after replay-safe Bedrock prompt aborts
target.body:
Closes #87876

AI-assisted: yes

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where users running long Bedrock agent sessions could lose the run when the Bedrock provider surfaced a provider-originated prompt abort. In the replay-safe prompt-abort shape from #87876, the run was marked aborted before the existing model fallback path could evaluate it, so configured fallback models were not tried.

## Why This Change Was Made

The change lets only replay-safe provider prompt aborts enter the existing prompt failover path. It keeps user/external aborts, session timeouts, compaction timeouts, tool-execution timeouts, and attempts with possible side effects out of fallback so intentional cancellation and unsafe replay behavior stay unchanged.

## User Impact

Bedrock users with configured fallback models can recover from this provider-originated prompt abort class instead of ending the whole agent run immediately. Runs that are not safe to replay still fail rather than duplicating side effects.

## Evidence

Source-level proof:

- `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/agents/embedded-agent-runner/run.prompt-timeout-fallback.test.ts src/agents/model-fallback.run-embedded.e2e.test.ts`
- Structured autoreview on `fix/bedrock-prompt-abort-fallback-87876`: clean, no accepted/actionable findings.

Live Bedrock proof attempts, July 3, 2026:

- AWS auth used profile-based resolution: `AWS_PROFILE` with `AWS_SDK_LOAD_CONFIG=1`. AWS key/session env was not exported to the child runs.
- Direct Bedrock model smoke passed: `node scripts/test-live.mjs --no-quiet -- src/agents/models.profiles.live.test.ts -t "completes across selected models"` with `OPENCLAW_LIVE_PROVIDERS=amazon-bedrock` and `OPENCLAW_LIVE_MODELS=amazon-bedrock/global.anthropic.claude-sonnet-4-6`.
- Gateway Bedrock smoke passed: `node scripts/test-live.mjs --no-quiet -- src/gateway/gateway-models.profiles.live.test.ts -t "runs meaningful prompts across models with available keys"` with `OPENCLAW_LIVE_GATEWAY_PROVIDERS=amazon-bedrock` and the same model. The prompt and tool-read probes both ended `stopReason=stop`.
- Issue-specific long probe with Bedrock primary plus `anthropic/claude-haiku-4-5` fallback, using a 66,188-byte replay-safe prompt: `runId=29d923a4-4014-471a-bfa4-a3d6d78a02c6`, `status=ok`, `stopReason=stop`; no `embedded run failover decision`, no `model fallback decision`, and no `This operation was aborted`.
- Second issue-specific heavy probe with the same primary/fallback, using a 74,382-byte prompt: `runId=2f21aaee-8341-4aab-a435-77735596e2f8`, `status=ok`, `stopReason=stop`; again no abort/fallback.

Proof gap:

- These live runs prove Bedrock and Gateway reachability from a local fixed checkout containing this runtime change plus the adjacent #99607 live-smoke harness fix, but the current AWS account/region did not reproduce the provider-originated abort envelope from #87876.
- There is still no after-fix real log showing `externalAbort=false`, replay-safe metadata, and the configured fallback model being attempted. Exact live proof needs either reporter/production-environment logs after this patch, or a maintainer decision to accept the source-level predicate/tests plus these negative live attempts.

target.title: Support Ultra thinking for the native Codex runtime
target.body:
## Summary

Adds `ultra` as a first-class thinking level for OpenClaw's **native Codex app-server runtime** when the live Codex model catalog advertises that level.

This is intentionally not a generic `ultra -> max` alias. Native Codex owns the full Ultra semantics: proactive multi-agent orchestration plus backend-compatible maximum inference effort. Embedded OpenClaw/provider runtimes that do not implement that orchestration do not advertise Ultra.

Legacy aliases remain stable: `ultrathink` continues to normalize to `high`; only explicit `ultra` selects the new tier.

## What Problem This Solves

OpenAI Codex PR <https://github.com/openai/codex/pull/29899> defines Ultra as a user-facing orchestration level:

- Codex Core selects `MultiAgentMode::Proactive`.
- Codex injects proactive delegation instructions and owns native sub-agent execution.
- At inference boundaries, Codex maps Ultra to the backend-compatible `max` effort.

Therefore OpenClaw should pass explicit `ultra` unchanged to the native Codex app-server, not flatten it to `max` itself. Other OpenClaw runtimes must not claim Ultra support merely because they can send `max`.

## Changes

- Add `ultra` to canonical thinking-level/session types needed to carry a native Codex selection.
- Preserve `ultrathink -> high` for backwards compatibility; explicit `ultra` is required.
- Expose Ultra only from the native Codex provider profile when live app-server discovery advertises it.
- Pass `effort: "ultra"` through native Codex `turn/start` and collaboration-mode settings.
- Keep embedded OpenClaw/OpenAI/Google/Anthropic provider profiles Ultra-free unless they separately implement equivalent orchestration semantics.
- Add tests for normalization, Codex profile discovery, native request payloads, unsupported-runtime rejection/clamping, and legacy alias behavior.
- Update thinking-level documentation with the native-Codex-only scope.

## Evidence

### Official semantics

OpenAI Codex PR <https://github.com/openai/codex/pull/29899> implements Ultra in Codex Core. Its source derives proactive multi-agent mode from `ReasoningEffort::Ultra`, injects proactive delegation instructions, and converts Ultra to `max` only at inference request boundaries.

### Real configured-provider behavior (sanitized)

Codex CLI 0.142.4 was configured with:

```toml
model = "gpt-5.6-sol"
model_reasoning_effort = "ultra"
```

Live model discovery advertised:

```text
gpt-5.6-sol: low, medium, high, xhigh, max, ultra
```

A real ephemeral read-only turn completed successfully:

```text
$ codex exec --ephemeral --skip-git-repo-check --sandbox read-only --json \
    'Reply exactly with ULTRA_OK_1424 and nothing else.'
...
item.completed: ULTRA_OK_1424
turn.completed
```

This proves the native Codex 0.142.4 runtime accepts and executes the Ultra selection. OpenClaw's responsibility is to preserve that selection across its native Codex bridge.


### Current-head native app-server bridge proof (sanitized, 2026-07-03)

A current-head OpenClaw bridge proof was run with a disposable app-server home and a non-default entitlement fixture. This is intentionally classified as `PASS_CONTAMINATED_ONLY`; it validates the native app-server entitlement and OpenClaw bridge behavior, not clean-stage default-profile behavior. Production Gateway state and production config were not used.

```text
head: 78fb055d
live model/list target: gpt-5.6-sol
live supportedReasoningEfforts: low, medium, high, xhigh, max, ultra
thread/start: accepted, model=gpt-5.6-sol
turn/start: accepted
captured turn/start.effort: ultra
captured turn/start.collaborationMode.settings.reasoning_effort: ultra
cleanup: copied entitlement fixture absent after run
verdict: APP_SERVER_BRIDGE_ULTRA_OK
```

This directly exercises current-head OpenClaw source constructing a real native Codex app-server `turn/start` request after live discovery advertised Ultra.

### OpenClaw validation

The revised branch passed:

```text
node scripts/run-vitest.mjs \
  src/auto-reply/thinking.test.ts \
  src/llm/model-utils.test.ts \
  src/config/config.schema-regressions.test.ts \
  extensions/codex/provider.test.ts \
  extensions/codex/src/app-server/thread-lifecycle.test.ts

# 198 focused tests passed, including 89 native Codex provider/turn tests

pnpm tsgo:core       # passed
pnpm tsgo:core:test  # passed
```

Additional OpenAI/Anthropic/Google/provider-stream safety suites passed after verifying that non-Codex profiles do not expose Ultra and stale internal Ultra values are handled defensively rather than forwarded as a claimed feature.

## Non-goals

- No generic Ultra profile exposure for embedded OpenClaw/provider runtimes.
- No claim that `max` alone is equivalent to Ultra. Defensive stale-value clamps in non-Codex transports are compatibility guards, not advertised Ultra support.
- No reimplementation of Codex proactive multi-agent policy inside OpenClaw; the native Codex app-server owns that behavior.

target.title: fix: antml:/mm: namespaced tool-call XML leaks into chat replies (#97750)
target.body:
Closes #97750

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where users on any deployment that serves a Claude model through an anthropic-messages-compatible proxy would see raw tool-call XML in their chat replies, and sometimes get no usable answer at all, when the proxy intermittently degraded a native `tool_use` block into plain text.

In that degraded case the model's tool call arrives as the Anthropic namespaced XML dialect — an optional `function_calls` wrapper containing `antml:invoke` / `antml:parameter` tags that use `name="..."` attributes (MiniMax emits the same shape with an `mm:` prefix). The harness did not recognize the namespace prefix or the attribute form anywhere, so the entire block leaked into the user-visible message instead of being executed, and a turn whose whole body was unrecognized markup could end with no real reply.

A follow-up fix in this PR also closes a streaming-only variant of the same leak: the final repair parser accepts whitespace-flexible attribute-dialect invoke tags (optional whitespace after `<`, around the `name` attribute, and around `=`), but the streamed-prefix recognizer only kept the exact `<ns>invoke name="` form buffered. A grammar-legal split form such as `<invoke name = "exec">` was therefore classified impossible mid-stream and flushed as raw visible text before final-message repair could promote it.

## Why This Change Was Made

The degraded tool call should never reach the user: it should either be executed or, failing that, hidden. This change teaches both layers that own that contract about the namespaced attribute dialect, using a closed namespace allow-list (`antml:`, `mm:`) factored into a single reused fragment — mirroring the existing reasoning-tag handling — so arbitrary `ns:` prefixes are not matched.

- Visible-text sanitizer: the tag-name scan now skips a known namespace prefix before reading the local tag name, and the quick-check / payload-start patterns accept the same optional prefix, so a namespaced wrapper is stripped on the same opt-in paths as the bare dialect.
- Repair/promotion layer: the repair grammar now promotes the attribute dialect (`invoke name="..."` / `parameter name="..."`, optionally namespaced, optionally wrapped in `function_calls`) back into an executed tool call, including the streaming and over-cap paths. Parameterless/self-closing invokes are never promoted, parameter values stay literal, and the existing payload-size limits are honored.
- Streaming-prefix recognizer: `isViableXmlishInvokeOpenPrefix` is rewritten as a phase scanner that mirrors the final parser grammar one token at a time, so a buffer that ends partway through any phase of a grammar-legal invoke open (including whitespace-split forms) stays buffered instead of leaking, while the existing tool-name gating is preserved unchanged.
- `stripPlainTextToolCallBlocks` gained an optional code-region predicate, threaded in from the delivery pipeline and `sanitizeUserFacingText`, so a complete invoke block inside a fenced or inline code span is no longer silently removed.

Non-goals/boundaries: the Anthropic and DSML transports are intentionally untouched (the native path is correct; the failure is degraded text owned by the repair package and sanitizer), no new public SDK surface is added, and no runtime fallback execution from sanitized text is introduced. The equals dialect (`<function=...>`/`<parameter=...>`), bracket, and Harmony paths are unchanged.

## User Impact

Users on proxied Claude routes no longer see raw `antml:` tool-call XML in their replies. When the proxy degrades a tool call to text, the call is now recovered and executed instead of leaking, so the turn produces a real result. This now also holds when the degraded tool call streams in a whitespace-flexible form split across chunks, which previously slipped past the streamed-prefix recognizer and leaked. Code examples that legitimately contain such tags inside code fences or inline code are preserved rather than stripped.

## Evidence

Focused unit tests cover both layers and the edge cases:

- Sanitizer: namespaced `function_calls`/`invoke`/`parameter` stripped to surrounding prose; truncated namespaced opening hidden; namespaced markup preserved inside fenced and inline code through the full delivery pipeline. Delivery-path regression coverage locks both directions across the `antml:`, `mm:`, and bare (no-namespace) prefixes: an unfenced standalone `invoke` block (and a pure standalone block with no surrounding prose) is stripped, while the same block inside a fenced code span is preserved verbatim, so the real leak shape is removed without over-scrubbing legitimate code examples.
- Promotion: a streamed namespaced attribute-dialect message promotes to a real tool call (including a split/chunked stream); a self-closing parameterless invoke is not promoted; mixed prose declines promotion; an arbitrary `foo:` namespace is neither promoted nor stripped (locks the closed allow-list); multiple invokes in one wrapper parse and strip correctly; a parameter value containing a literal close marker is extracted to the first close.
- Streaming-prefix recognizer: whitespace-split attribute-dialect invoke opens (spaces around the `name` attribute and `=`, including the open tag split across stream chunks at the whitespace boundaries, for both `antml:` and bare namespaces and a single-quote variant) stay buffered and promote to a tool call instead of leaking.
- Argument-less invoke followed by prose: a complete zero-parameter (`<invoke name="read"></invoke>\nHello`) or self-closing (`<invoke name="read"/>\nHello`) invoke followed by visible prose no longer leaks the raw invoke XML in streamed output — the invoke markup is stripped and only the prose (`Hello`) is delivered, with no tool call promoted, across `antml:`, `mm:`, and bare prefixes and split-across-chunks streams. Regression coverage also locks the final-message shapes where the invoke and prose arrive as separate text content blocks, and where a single leading content block carries both the invoke and its trailing prose, so the visible prose is preserved exactly once with no duplication or loss; a pure argument-less invoke with no prose still scrubs to an empty message; and a parametered invoke with no prose still promotes to a tool call (positive lock).

Real-behavior proof (Docker, redacted): a self-contained harness under `proof/pr-97845/` drives the actual stream normalizer through the same option wiring the provider-stream wrapper uses, feeding a degraded provider stream that emits a whitespace-split invoke open (`<invoke name = "exec">...`) split across chunks at the whitespace boundaries. Captured runtime output shows the regression and its fix:

With the recognizer reverted to its previous literal-prefix form (BEFORE), the split open leaks as visible text:

```
fake upstream chunks: ["<invoke"," name"," ="," \"exec\">","<parameter name=\"command\">echo demo</parameter>","</invoke>"]
emitted events:
  [1] text_delta "<invoke"
  [2] text_delta " name"
  [3] text_delta " ="
  [4] text_delta " \"exec\">"
  [5] text_delta "<parameter name=\"command\">echo demo</parameter>"
  [6] text_delta "</invoke>"
  [7] toolcall_start ...
visible text emitted to user: "<invoke name = \"exec\"><parameter name=\"command\">echo demo</parameter></invoke>"
VERDICT: LEAK
```

With the fix in place (AFTER), the same bytes stay buffered and promote to a tool call with no visible leak:

```
emitted events:
  [0] toolcall_start
  [1] toolcall_delta {"command":"echo demo"}
  [2] done reason=toolUse  toolCall name=exec arguments={"command":"echo demo"}
visible text emitted to user: ""
VERDICT: NO LEAK
```

The captured output above is the redacted before/after runtime evidence; the synthetic stream reproduction needs no provider key. (The proof was produced with a Docker harness that drives the real stream normalizer through the provider-stream wrapper; per review feedback it is kept here in the description rather than committed to the branch.)

Local validation:

```
node scripts/test-projects.mjs (affected test files): pass (sanitizer + promotion + agents)
vitest src/plugin-sdk/provider-stream-shared.test.ts: 92 pass (incl. new whitespace-split and argument-less-invoke-plus-prose regressions)
pnpm tsgo:core && pnpm tsgo:core:test: clean
oxlint on changed source files: 0 warnings, 0 errors
oxfmt --check on changed files: all correctly formatted
```

target.title: fix(barnacle): resync candidate labels on ready_for_review, remove stale labels
target.body:
## Summary

- Problem: Barnacle auto-response doesn't resync candidate labels when a draft PR is marked `ready_for_review`, leaving stale candidate labels (e.g. `triage: blank-template`) on PRs with meaningful bodies.
- Why it matters: Draft PRs auto-labeled with `triage: blank-template` keep that label after the author fills in the template and clicks "Ready for review", confusing triage workflow.
- What changed: Added `ready_for_review` to the auto-response workflow trigger and script allowlist; rewrote `applyPullRequestCandidateLabels` to compute and remove stale candidate labels while preserving suppression/privileged-author guards.
- What did NOT change: No changes to existing candidate label classification rules, maintainer/OWNER skip logic, or `bad-barnacle` suppression.

## Change Type (select all)

- [x] Bug fix
- [x] CI/CD / infra

## Scope (select all touched areas)

- [x] CI/CD / infra

## Linked Issue/PR

- Closes #77343
- [x] This PR fixes a bug or regression

## Root Cause (if applicable)

- Root cause: Three gaps — (1) `.github/workflows/auto-response.yml` did not include `ready_for_review` in `pull_request_target` types, (2) `isPrCandidateEvent` allowlist in `barnacle-auto-response.mjs` did not include `ready_for_review`, and (3) `applyPullRequestCandidateLabels` was add-only (never removed stale labels).
- Missing detection / guardrail: No test for the `ready_for_review` → stale label removal path.
- Contributing context (if known): N/A

## Real behavior proof

Not applicable — this PR modifies only GitHub Actions workflow automation (`.github/workflows/auto-response.yml`).
No product code, CLI, gateway, plugin, or UI surface is touched.
Barnacle + changelog unit tests cover the changed logic (30/30 + 15/15 passed).

## Regression Test Plan (if applicable)

- Coverage level that should have caught this:
  - [x] Unit test
- Target test or file: `test/scripts/barnacle-auto-response.test.ts`
- Scenario the test should lock in: `ready_for_review` action removes stale candidate labels when PR body becomes meaningful
- Why this is the smallest reliable guardrail: Directly exercises `applyPullRequestCandidateLabels` return value + `removeLabels` call path
- Existing test that already covers this (if any): None — this was a new coverage gap
- If no new test is added, why not: N/A

## User-visible / Behavior Changes

When a maintainer-owned PR transitions from draft to `ready_for_review` (or is edited), Barnacle recomputes candidate labels and removes any stale Barnacle-owned candidate labels (e.g. `triage: blank-template`) that no longer match the PR body/files.

## Diagram (if applicable)

```text
Before:
[PR ready_for_review] -> [add missing labels only] -> [stale labels persist]

After:
[PR ready_for_review] -> [recompute labels] -> [add missing + remove stale] -> [labels match body]
```

## Security Impact (required)

- New permissions/capabilities? (`Yes/No`) No
- Secrets/tokens handling changed? (`Yes/No`) No
- New/changed network calls? (`Yes/No`) No (existing GitHub API calls)
- Command/tool execution surface changed? (`Yes/No`) No
- Data access scope changed? (`Yes/No`) No

## Repro + Verification

### Environment

- OS: any (GitHub Actions)
- Runtime/container: Node 24 (GitHub Actions)
- Model/provider: N/A
- Integration/channel: GitHub auto-response workflow

### Steps

1. Open a draft PR with a blank issue template body
2. Barnacle auto-labels it with `triage: blank-template`
3. Edit body to fill in the template (Problem/Why/What)
4. Click "Ready for review"

### Expected

- `triage: blank-template` is removed; correct candidate labels applied

### Actual

- `triage: blank-template` persisted (before fix)

## Evidence

- [x] Failing test/log before + passing after

## Human Verification (required)

- Verified scenarios: `ready_for_review` with meaningful body removes stale labels; `ready_for_review` recomputes candidate labels; `bad-barnacle` suppresses removal; maintainer-authored PRs not mutated
- Edge cases checked: `bad-barnacle` suppression, maintainer/OWNER/COLLABORATOR skip, mixed candidate label transitions
- What you did **not** verify: Live GitHub workflow run (requires merge to test end-to-end)

## Compatibility / Migration

- Backward compatible? (`Yes`)
- Config/env changes? (`No`)
- Migration needed? (`No`)

## Risks and Mitigations

- Risk: Stale label removal could incorrectly strip a label if `classifyPullRequestCandidateLabels` has a bug.
  - Mitigation: Removal only targets Barnacle-owned candidate labels (`candidateLabelValues`); `bad-barnacle` and privileged-author skips preserved; full test suite covers all paths.

target.title: improve: reduce repeated session startup scans
target.body:
Related: #99190

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where long-lived session transcripts could still be touched with full-file scans on run startup paths even when only the first JSONL header line was needed, and where large AGENTS.md bootstrap content could be re-scanned for the same policy digest every turn.

## Why This Change Was Made

This keeps the no-assistant session reset guard bounded to the first non-empty transcript header line instead of reading the full JSONL file, while preserving the existing fail-closed behavior for corrupt headers, including blank-prefixed transcripts. It also caches AGENTS.md policy digests by content hash and budget so unchanged bootstrap content avoids repeated line splitting and policy-candidate scanning.

This intentionally does not replace SessionManager cold-open parsing with a tail-only reader yet; that path also restores model/thinking state, retained compaction tails, leaf controls, labels, and mutation-safe transcript state, so it needs a separate indexed or equivalence-proven design.

AI-assisted: yes.

## User Impact

Users with long-running agent sessions should see less avoidable pre-LLM file work in startup/bootstrap paths. Behavior is unchanged for session reset safety and bootstrap prompt output.

## Evidence

- node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/agents/embedded-agent-runner/session-manager-init.test.ts
  - 8 passed, including blank-prefixed corrupt-header and capped blank-prefix preservation coverage.
- node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/agents/embedded-agent-helpers.buildbootstrapcontextfiles.test.ts
  - 24 passed.

target.title: fix(commitments): stop hardcoding fastMode in extraction (#78451)
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves
MiniMax Coding Plan users whose token plan includes `MiniMax-M2.7` but not `MiniMax-M2.7-highspeed` could not run commitment extraction because the hidden extraction path hardcoded `fastMode: true`, silently rewriting the selected model to the unsupported highspeed variant.

## Evidence
The PR body documents the failing path: `src/commitments/runtime.ts` passed `fastMode: true` into `runEmbeddedPiAgent`, and `src/agents/pi-embedded-runner/minimax-stream-wrappers.ts` rewrote the model id to `-highspeed`. The fix removes the hardcoded fast mode for commitment extraction so the user's configured model stays unchanged.

---

## Summary

MiniMax Coding Plan operators whose plan owns `MiniMax-M2.7` but not the `-highspeed` variant hit `HTTP 500: your current token plan not support model, MiniMax-M2.7-highspeed (2061)` on every commitment extraction pass, because the commitments extraction path passed `fastMode: true` unconditionally to `runEmbeddedPiAgent`, which caused the MiniMax stream wrapper's `createMinimaxFastModeWrapper` to rewrite the base model id to `MiniMax-M2.7-highspeed`.

## Root Cause

- `src/commitments/runtime.ts:242` (pre-fix): the call to `runEmbeddedPiAgent` for hidden commitment extraction hardcoded `fastMode: true`.
- `src/agents/pi-embedded-runner/minimax-stream-wrappers.ts:24`: the MiniMax stream wrapper accepts a `fastMode` boolean and, when true, swaps the base model id to its `-highspeed` variant.
- Result: every commitments extraction request silently flipped `MiniMax-M2.7` → `MiniMax-M2.7-highspeed`, which Coding Plan operators do not own. MiniMax responds with HTTP 500 / error code 2061. Reporter verified the Coding Plan owns the base model but not highspeed.
- The reporter listed three valid fix shapes (drop the hardcode, add a config field, or inherit agent fastMode). This PR uses option 1: dropping the hardcode lets the existing `resolveFastModeState` helper continue to control fast-mode for the rest of the agent runtime, and commitments extraction inherits the same default-false behavior.

## Changes

- `src/commitments/runtime.ts`: remove `fastMode: true` from the `runEmbeddedPiAgent` payload built in the commitments extraction path. Add a comment explaining the reason so this does not regress.
- `src/commitments/runtime.test.ts`: extend the existing `runEmbeddedPiAgentMock` assertion to assert `fastMode` is **not** in the payload, locking in the regression fix.
- `CHANGELOG.md`: single-line entry under Unreleased / Fixes.

## Real behavior proof

- Behavior addressed: On every commitment extraction pass, MiniMax Coding Plan operators receive `HTTP 500: your current token plan not support model, MiniMax-M2.7-highspeed (2061)` from the MiniMax server because the agent runtime requested `MiniMax-M2.7-highspeed` even though their plan only owns `MiniMax-M2.7`. target.title: fix(qa-lab): bound suite runtime gateway JSON response reads
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

`extensions/qa-lab/src/suite-runtime-gateway.ts` used an unbounded
`await response.json()` on the gateway HTTP success path inside `fetchJson`.
A misbehaving or hostile gateway endpoint (or accidental huge payload) could
stream oversized JSON and trigger unbounded allocation during `JSON.parse`
while QA Lab suite scenarios read config snapshots or apply config patches
over the local gateway transport.

Replacing the success read with `readProviderJsonResponse` caps JSON parsing at
16 MiB and emits labeled errors such as
`qa-lab-suite-fetch-json: JSON response exceeds 16777216 bytes`.

This aligns QA Lab's suite runtime gateway with the broader OpenClaw
response-limit campaign that already bounded sibling provider and channel
surfaces (Telegram plugin Bot API reads, Copilot token exchange, Google OAuth,
QA Lab Telegram live transport, etc.).

## Changes

* `extensions/qa-lab/src/suite-runtime-gateway.ts`:
  - imports `readProviderJsonResponse` from `openclaw/plugin-sdk/provider-http`
  - replaces `await response.json()` with
    `readProviderJsonResponse(response, "qa-lab-suite-fetch-json")` in
    `fetchJson`

* `extensions/qa-lab/src/suite-runtime-gateway.test.ts`:
  - adds regression test `bounds oversized suite gateway JSON responses` using a
    real `Response` object and asserting the labeled cap error

* `scripts/proof-qa-lab-suite-gateway-bound.mjs`:
  - path-level proof over `node:http` streaming gateway envelopes plus vitest
    regression hook

## Real behavior proof

**Behavior addressed:** Oversized gateway JSON success bodies fail closed
instead of unbounded `JSON.parse` allocation on the QA Lab suite runtime
gateway path.

**Real environment tested:** Node v22.22.0, macOS 15.3.1, `node:http` streaming
server on `127.0.0.1`, built helper from `dist/plugin-sdk/provider-http.js`.

**Exact steps:**
1. Stream an ~18 MiB gateway `{ payload: ... }` envelope from a local HTTP
   server (no `Content-Length`).
2. Drive `readProviderJsonResponse` with label `qa-lab-suite-fetch-json` → assert
   labeled parse cap.
3. Drive the same helper on a buffered >16 MiB envelope (post-fetch handoff shape).
4. Verify a normal config snapshot envelope still parses.
5. Negative control: unbounded `response.json()` on a 64×1 MiB injected stream
   consumes all chunks without canceling.
6. Bounded helper cancels early on the same injected stream.
7. Run qa-lab vitest regression via `fetchJson("http://127.0.0.1:43123/config")`.

**Observed result:**
- Parse boundary (stream): `qa-lab-suite-fetch-json: JSON response exceeds 16777216 bytes`
- Buffered oversized envelope: 16 778 254 bytes rejected before `JSON.parse`
- Normal config snapshot envelope parses with hash intact
- Negative control: unbounded `.json()` read all 64 chunks; bounded helper stopped at
  readCount=17 and invoked `cancel()`
- `ALL PROOF ASSERTIONS PASSED`

**What was not tested:** live QA Lab suite runs against a real OpenClaw gateway process.

## Evidence

```
=== QA Lab suite gateway bound proof (path-level) ===
--- Case 1: oversized streamed gateway body rejected at parse boundary ---
  ok: readProviderJsonResponse rejects oversized streamed gateway body
  ok: parse-boundary label present (got: qa-lab-suite-fetch-json: JSON response exceeds 16777216 bytes)

--- Case 2: oversized buffered gateway envelope (production handoff) ---
  ok: buffered oversized gateway body rejected before JSON.parse
  ok: body size 16778254 bytes exceeds 16777216 cap

--- Case 3: normal gateway config snapshot still parses ---
  ok: config snapshot envelope parses
  ok: config object intact

--- Case 4: negative control — unbounded response.json() ---
  ok: unbounded .json() consumed all 64 chunks (readCount=64)
  ok: stream NOT cancelled via .cancel()

--- Case 5: bounded helper cancels oversized injected stream ---
  ok: readProviderJsonResponse rejected oversized injected stream
  ok: stream read stopped early (readCount=17)
  ok: stream cancel() was invoked

--- Case 6: qa-lab suite gateway regression test ---
  Tests  1 passed | 12 skipped (13)
  ok: vitest qa-lab suite gateway bound regression test passed

ALL PROOF ASSERTIONS PASSED
```

```
OPENCLAW_VITEST_MAX_WORKERS=1 pnpm test \
  extensions/qa-lab/src/suite-runtime-gateway.test.ts \
  -t "bounds oversized suite gateway JSON responses"
# Tests  1 passed | 12 skipped (13)
```

New bound regression test (1 added):
- `bounds oversized suite gateway JSON responses` ✓

## Summary

This PR tightens the existing compatible-bundle MCP path for bundles that need a narrower default tool surface.

- Adds regression coverage that a Codex-compatible bundle `.mcp.json` preserves `toolFilter.include`, `toolFilter.exclude`, and a relative bundle data root.
- Documents bundle MCP tool filters on the plugin-bundles page alongside the existing transport and tool-naming guidance.
- Keeps scope limited to bundle MCP loading/docs; runtime filtering behavior already exists and is covered separately.

Reviewers should focus on whether the bundle MCP docs accurately describe the existing runtime behavior and whether the new compatible-bundle regression is useful.

## Linked context

No issue filed.

Related precedent investigated: bundle MCP support and follow-up coverage in prior OpenClaw PRs such as #48611, #71287, #79686, and #88399. This PR follows that existing bundle MCP seam.

## Summary
- The runtime already walks `memory/` recursively via `collectMemoryFilesFromDir` (`packages/memory-host-sdk/src/host/internal.ts`), so nested files like `memory/YYYY-MM/YYYY-MM-DD.md` are indexed and searched. But several agent-facing descriptors and public docs still said `memory/*.md`, which can mislead agents into thinking the index is flat.
- This PR updates the remaining stale references to `memory/**/*.md`. No runtime behavior change.

## Files touched
- `extensions/memory-core/index.ts` — lazy `memory_search` / `memory_get` descriptors
- `extensions/memory-core/src/tools.ts` — concrete `memory_search` / `memory_get` descriptions
- `extensions/memory-core/src/prompt-section.ts` — system-prompt recall guidance
- `src/config/schema.help.ts` — `agents.defaults.memorySearch` help text
- `docs/concepts/memory-builtin.md`, `memory.md`, `system-prompt.md`
- `docs/gateway/config-agents.md`, `docs/reference/token-use.md`
- `docs/.generated/config-baseline.sha256` regenerated via `pnpm config:docs:gen`

## Note
This supersedes #72748. That PR also carried QMD watcher changes that were independently resolved upstream by #81802 (`watch-settle.ts`), so the surviving value was just this wording alignment. Splitting it out as a small, behavior-neutral PR for easier review.

## Real behavior proof

**Behavior or issue addressed**: Agent-facing descriptors and public docs said `memory/*.md` even though the runtime already walks `memory/` recursively and indexes nested files such as `memory/YYYY-MM/YYYY-MM-DD.md`. This PR aligns the wording to `memory/**/*.md` so agents and readers see what is actually indexed. The change is wording-only; the proof below shows (a) the installed runtime already exhibits the recursive behavior the new wording describes, and (b) the after-patch descriptor and prompt strings on this branch actually carry the new `memory/**/*.md` wording when imported at runtime.

**Observed result after fix**: (a) The freshly written nested file `memory/2026-05/2026-05-24-recursive-proof.md` (two levels deep under `memory/`) was indexed by `openclaw memory index` and returned as the top match (score `0.812`) for the unique token. target.title: fix(commitments): stop hardcoding fastMode in extraction (#78451)
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves
MiniMax Coding Plan users whose token plan includes `MiniMax-M2.7` but not `MiniMax-M2.7-highspeed` could not run commitment extraction because the hidden extraction path hardcoded `fastMode: true`, silently rewriting the selected model to the unsupported highspeed variant.

## Evidence
The PR body documents the failing path: `src/commitments/runtime.ts` passed `fastMode: true` into `runEmbeddedPiAgent`, and `src/agents/pi-embedded-runner/minimax-stream-wrappers.ts` rewrote the model id to `-highspeed`. The fix removes the hardcoded fast mode for commitment extraction so the user's configured model stays unchanged.

---

## Summary

MiniMax Coding Plan operators whose plan owns `MiniMax-M2.7` but not the `-highspeed` variant hit `HTTP 500: your current token plan not support model, MiniMax-M2.7-highspeed (2061)` on every commitment extraction pass, because the commitments extraction path passed `fastMode: true` unconditionally to `runEmbeddedPiAgent`, which caused the MiniMax stream wrapper's `createMinimaxFastModeWrapper` to rewrite the base model id to `MiniMax-M2.7-highspeed`.

## Root Cause

- `src/commitments/runtime.ts:242` (pre-fix): the call to `runEmbeddedPiAgent` for hidden commitment extraction hardcoded `fastMode: true`.
- `src/agents/pi-embedded-runner/minimax-stream-wrappers.ts:24`: the MiniMax stream wrapper accepts a `fastMode` boolean and, when true, swaps the base model id to its `-highspeed` variant.
- Result: every commitments extraction request silently flipped `MiniMax-M2.7` → `MiniMax-M2.7-highspeed`, which Coding Plan operators do not own. MiniMax responds with HTTP 500 / error code 2061. Reporter verified the Coding Plan owns the base model but not highspeed.
- The reporter listed three valid fix shapes (drop the hardcode, add a config field, or inherit agent fastMode). This PR uses option 1: dropping the hardcode lets the existing `resolveFastModeState` helper continue to control fast-mode for the rest of the agent runtime, and commitments extraction inherits the same default-false behavior.

## Changes

- `src/commitments/runtime.ts`: remove `fastMode: true` from the `runEmbeddedPiAgent` payload built in the commitments extraction path. Add a comment explaining the reason so this does not regress.
- `src/commitments/runtime.test.ts`: extend the existing `runEmbeddedPiAgentMock` assertion to assert `fastMode` is **not** in the payload, locking in the regression fix.
- `CHANGELOG.md`: single-line entry under Unreleased / Fixes.

## Real behavior proof

- Behavior addressed: On every commitment extraction pass, MiniMax Coding Plan operators receive `HTTP 500: your current token plan not support model, MiniMax-M2.7-highspeed (2061)` from the MiniMax server because the agent runtime requested `MiniMax-M2.7-highspeed` even though their plan only owns `MiniMax-M2.7`. The reporter (`@advaitpaliwal`) verified `commitments.enabled: true, commitments.maxPerDay: 10` config, then ran a real Coding Plan session, observed extraction always selecting the highspeed variant, and traced the root cause to `dist/runtime-CXt7BFiH.js` line 386 (`fastMode: true` hardcoded). Issue: https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/78451
- Real environment tested: Local OpenClaw checkout at `../openclaw-78451` on Windows 11 + Node 22.14. The smoke script reads the **patched production file `src/commitments/runtime.ts` directly from the worktree**, locates the entire `defaultExtractBatch` function (the path that builds the `runEmbeddedPiAgent` payload), prints its SHA-256 + verbatim bytes, then runs structural assertions over the captured payload literal to prove `fastMode: true` is gone, the `#78451` explanatory comment is in place, and every sibling field is preserved. No mocks, no test runner — the patched source bytes drive the smoke. PR head: `a3189f329687fa8c2c9da783afbc0d644ea94573`.
- Exact steps or command run after this patch: `git checkout fix/commitments-no-fastmode-hardcode && node --experimental-strip-types ./smoke-pr78459.mts`, where `smoke-pr78459.mts` reads `src/commitments/runtime.ts`, slices the `async function defaultExtractBatch` body, hashes it, prints the verbatim payload object literal, and runs structural assertions against the live patched source.
- Evidence after fix: Terminal output captured locally on PR head `a3189f3296` (Windows 11 + Node 22.14, the patched `src/commitments/runtime.ts` `defaultExtractBatch` function read from the worktree, 1660 bytes, SHA-256 `ae3690fc3189a7bc3e6d33e8693a3a28aa24ee3c7a82822618c5f1c762bcb379`).

~~~text
$ node --experimental-strip-types ./smoke-pr78459.mts
=== Patched defaultExtractBatch function — bytes from src/commitments/runtime.ts ===
offset: 7245 -> 8905 ( 1660 bytes)
SHA-256: ae3690fc3189a7bc3e6d33e8693a3a28aa24ee3c7a82822618c5f1c762bcb379

function body still contains literal 'fastMode: true': false
explanatory '#78451' comment present                : true
  preserved field 'disableTools: true': true
  preserved field 'thinkLevel: "off"': true
  preserved field 'verboseLevel: "off"': true
  preserved field 'reasoningLevel: "off"': true

=== Payload object passed to runEmbeddedPiAgent (verbatim from patched code) ===
{ cfg, agentId: first.agentId });
  const result = await runEmbeddedPiAgent({
    sessionId: runId,
    sessionKey: `agent:${first.agentId}:commitments:${runId}`,
    agentId: first.agentId,
    trigger: "manual",
    sessionFile: resolveExtractionSessionFile(first.agentId, runId),
    workspaceDir: resolveAgentWorkspaceDir(cfg, first.agentId),
    config: cfg,
    provider: modelRef.provider,
    model: modelRef.model,
    prompt: buildCommitmentExtractionPrompt({ cfg, items: params.items }),
    disableTools: true,
    thinkLevel: "off",
    verboseLevel: "off",
    reasoningLevel: "off",
    // Do not hardcode fastMode here: leaving the field undefined lets the
    // commitments extraction inherit the configured fast-mode state (which
    // defaults to false). Hardcoding true caused MiniMax Coding Plans without
    // highspeed access to fail with HTTP 500 because the MiniMax stream wrapper
    // would rewrite MiniMax-M2.7 -> MiniMax-M2.7-highspeed (#78451).
    timeoutMs: resolved.extraction.timeoutSeconds * 1000,
    runId,
    bootstrapContextMode: "lightweight",
    skillsSnapshot: { prompt: "", skills: [] },
    suppressToolErrorWarnings: true,
  }

=== fastMode-related lines in the payload (BEFORE-vs-AFTER comparison) ===
  // Do not hardcode fastMode here: leaving the field undefined lets the
  // highspeed access to fail with HTTP 500 because the MiniMax stream wrapper
  // would rewrite MiniMax-M2.7 -> MiniMax-M2.7-highspeed (#78451).
~~~

- Observed result after fix: The patched `defaultExtractBatch` function — pinned by a 1660-byte / SHA-256 `ae3690fc3189a7bc3e6d33e8693a3a28aa24ee3c7a82822618c5f1c762bcb379` integrity check — has zero `fastMode: true` literals (`function body still contains literal 'fastMode: true': false`). The explanatory `#78451` comment is in place (`explanatory '#78451' comment present: true`), and every sibling field (`disableTools: true`, `thinkLevel: "off"`, `verboseLevel: "off"`, `reasoningLevel: "off"`) is preserved verbatim. The captured payload literal shown verbatim above confirms `runEmbeddedPiAgent` is now called without a `fastMode` key — so the MiniMax stream wrapper at `src/agents/pi-embedded-runner/minimax-stream-wrappers.ts:24` no longer flips `MiniMax-M2.7` → `MiniMax-M2.7-highspeed`, and the operator's configured base model id flows through unchanged.
- What was not tested: A live HTTP roundtrip against the real MiniMax server with a Coding Plan token is not available on the contributor machine, so this is source-level / structural proof against the patched payload-builder, not a live MiniMax 200 response. Maintainers may apply `proof: override` if a live MiniMax recording is required; the reporter's original issue already contains live HTTP 500 evidence from the real Coding Plan.

## Test

- `pnpm test src/commitments/runtime.test.ts` — 6 passed (including the new `expect(callArgs).not.toHaveProperty("fastMode")` regression assertion).

## Notes

- Scope: smallest complete fix. No new config surface and no provider/wrapper edits — the existing fast-mode resolution chain already covers the right behavior; the hardcode was the only thing forcing `true`.
- Compatibility: agents that need fast-mode for commitments can still set it via `agents.defaults.models.<id>.params.fastMode: true` (or per-agent `fastModeDefault: true`) — the `resolveFastModeState` chain is unchanged.

Closes #78451

target.title: improve: reduce repeated session startup scans
target.body:
Related: #99190

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where long-lived session transcripts could still be touched with full-file scans on run startup paths even when only the first JSONL header line was needed, and where large AGENTS.md bootstrap content could be re-scanned for the same policy digest every turn.

## Why This Change Was Made

This keeps the no-assistant session reset guard bounded to the first non-empty transcript header line instead of reading the full JSONL file, while preserving the existing fail-closed behavior for corrupt headers, including blank-prefixed transcripts. It also caches AGENTS.md policy digests by content hash and budget so unchanged bootstrap content avoids repeated line splitting and policy-candidate scanning.

This intentionally does not replace SessionManager cold-open parsing with a tail-only reader yet; that path also restores model/thinking state, retained compaction tails, leaf controls, labels, and mutation-safe transcript state, so it needs a separate indexed or equivalence-proven design.

AI-assisted: yes.

## User Impact

Users with long-running agent sessions should see less avoidable pre-LLM file work in startup/bootstrap paths. Behavior is unchanged for session reset safety and bootstrap prompt output.

## Evidence

- node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/agents/embedded-agent-runner/session-manager-init.test.ts
  - 8 passed, including blank-prefixed corrupt-header and capped blank-prefix preservation coverage.
